description: The two Pi-hole DNS servers (apps/pihole): whether each answers DNS, queries per second, blocked share, query types, upstreams, top clients, and the load on its host, with its FTL log. Queries come from the Pi-hole v6 API, the DNS probe from the cluster, host load from node_exporter on each Pi-hole.

panels.title: DNS answering
panels.description: A DNS query for example.com sent from the cluster to the Pi-hole (blackbox probe, every 15 s). This is what a client sees. Red means clients get no DNS from it.

panels.title: Host up
panels.description: Whether the Pi-hole host answers node_exporter on port 9100. Red with the DNS probe still answering means only the metrics path is down.

panels.title: Queries per second
panels.description: Queries per second over the last full 10 minutes. Usual is a few. The alert is above 30 for 15 minutes.

panels.title: DNS answer time
panels.description: How long the Pi-hole took to answer the probe query. A cached answer takes milliseconds. The alert is above 0.5 s for 10 minutes.

panels.title: Load per core
panels.description: Five minute load average divided by the number of cores. The alert is above 1.5 for 10 minutes.

panels.title: Memory available
panels.description: Share of the host memory that is available. The alert is under 10% for 10 minutes.

panels.title: Queries (last 24 h)
panels.description: Total queries in the period Pi-hole reports its summary for (the last 24 hours).

panels.title: Blocked
panels.description: Share of queries Pi-hole blocked.

panels.title: Blocking
panels.description: Whether Pi-hole blocking is enabled. Off means it was disabled in the interface or by a timer.

panels.title: Active clients
panels.description: Distinct clients that sent a query in the last 24 hours.

panels.title: Cache hit share
panels.description: Share of queries answered from FTL's cache.

panels.title: Domains on blocklist
panels.description: Domains in gravity (the blocklists).

panels.title: Queries per second
panels.description: Average queries per second over each 10 minute slot (solid) and Pi-hole's own current rate (FTL's frequency).

panels.title: Queries and blocked, per 10 minutes
panels.description: Queries Pi-hole handled in each 10 minute slot, and how many it blocked.

panels.title: Blocked share
panels.description: Share of queries blocked.

panels.title: Query types
panels.description: Queries by type over the summary period. A burst of one type (HTTPS, PTR, ANY) points at a client or a loop.

panels.title: Replies
panels.description: Replies by kind. A rise in serv_fail, refused or nx_domain means upstream or client trouble.

panels.title: Load average
panels.description: 1, 5 and 15 minute load average.

panels.title: CPU busy
panels.description: Share of CPU time that is not idle.

panels.title: Memory used
panels.description: Share of memory that is not available.

panels.title: DNS answer time
panels.description: Time to answer the probe query, per Pi-hole.

panels.title: Network traffic
panels.description: Receive (positive) and transmit (negative) on the Pi-hole host, loopback left out.

panels.title: Disk used
panels.description: Share of the root file system in use.

panels.title: Top clients
panels.description: Clients with the most queries over the summary period, per Pi-hole. The first row is the one to look at when the query rate is high.

panels.title: Upstream response time
panels.description: How long each upstream (forward destination) takes to answer Pi-hole.

panels.title: Queries by upstream
panels.description: Queries Pi-hole forwarded, by upstream.

panels.title: Up and answering
panels.description: History of the DNS probe and the host scrape. Red is a Pi-hole that did not answer.

panels.title: Query log lines
panels.description: Lines of pihole.log (app pihole-dns) in the time range: one per query and reply.

targets.expr: hostname:~`^${pihole:regex}$` app_name:=pihole-dns | stats count() as lines

panels.title: FTL log lines
panels.description: Lines of FTL.log (app pihole-FTL) in the time range.

targets.expr: hostname:~`^${pihole:regex}$` app_name:=pihole-FTL | stats count() as lines

panels.title: FTL warnings and errors
panels.description: FTL.log lines that carry WARNING, ERROR or CRIT. Rate limiting, a locked database and a failed gravity update show up here.

targets.expr: hostname:~`^${pihole:regex}$` app_name:=pihole-FTL ~"WARNING|ERROR|CRIT" | stats count() as lines

panels.title: Rate limited
panels.description: FTL.log lines about a client hitting the rate limit (RATE_LIMIT).

targets.expr: hostname:~`^${pihole:regex}$` app_name:=pihole-FTL "RATE_LIMIT" | stats count() as lines

panels.title: FTL log
panels.description: FTL.log, newest first. Startup, restarts, rate limiting, database and gravity events. The query log (pihole.log) is app pihole-dns in the Logs dashboard.
